title: Show and Tell
strapline: Something precious from home, and a room that listens — the first real experience of an audience.
intent: Children build confidence speaking in front of others about something they genuinely care about.
Bringing something from home builds the bridge between family life and nursery life.
Listening to a friend and asking them a question is real, purposeful listening practice.
Children practise sequencing a small account — what it is, where it came from, why it matters.
Every child gets a turn at being the one who is listened to.
implementation: Invite children to bring in a special item — a toy, a photo, a book, a shell from a holiday.
Keep the group small; five children listening properly beats twenty half-listening.
Sit the speaker somewhere clearly the speaker's place, so the role is visible.
Prompt with questions rather than taking over the telling — the words should be theirs.
Teach the audience to ask one question each, and model a good one first.
Have a spare basket of nursery treasures so a child who forgot is never left out.
Celebrate effort over polish — a one-word answer from a quiet child is a win.
key_questions: What have you brought to show us today?
Where did it come from, and who gave it to you?
What do you like best about it?
What would you like to ask about your friend's thing?
Can you tell us what happened when you got it?

impact.text: Children develop confidence in speaking to a group and are understood.
Children recount a real event from their own life in rough sequence.
Children listen and respond in a small group and hold their attention on a speaker.
Children ask real questions of each other and expect real answers.
Children grow in confidence in groups and contribute their own ideas.
Children talk about their own family and are interested that others differ.

enhancements: A themed week — something old, something you made, something from a journey.
A photo of each item added to a class book of "our treasures".
A recording station so a shy child can record their telling privately and play it.
A drawing table where listeners draw the object they have just heard about.
A parent invitation to send in a photo and a sentence for children who forget.
A "question of the week" the audience practises asking well.

playing_exploring: Children choose what to bring, so the whole thing starts from their interest.
Handling and showing a real object anchors the talk in something concrete.
active_learning: Speaking to a group takes courage, and children build it turn by turn.
Children keep going through nerves to finish what they wanted to say.
creating_thinking: Children decide what is worth saying and in what order.
Listeners frame a genuine question, which is real thinking about someone else.
